text:
Sasha: Heads-up — eu-west GPU pool hit a saturation wave ~09:12 UTC, shedder started returning 429s for some long-context batches. Clients without admission hints retried aggressively and amplified the tail.
Maya: Ugh. Any spike in request size distribution or a deployment? :thinking_face:
Sasha: No deploy at that time. Pattern looks like lots of medium-length chat (2–4k tokens) + a couple of huge rerank jobs. GPU slot churn + slow evictions caused queue depth to balloon.
infra-bot: [ALERT] region=eu-west pool=gpu-large saturation=HIGH at 2025-06-07T09:13:02Z (alert_id: sat-eu-1755)
Liam: We're seeing 429 vs 503 inconsistencies across edge nodes. Some nodes tell clients to retry, others drop. Need a consistent client signal so SDKs can back off with discipline.
Maya: +1. What do we want in the header? queue depth, estimated admit window, and maybe a hint for preferred fallback region?
Sasha: Proposal (for discussion):
- X-Redwood-Queue-Depth: current number of queued tasks on the target pool
- X-Redwood-Avg-Admit-Ms: moving avg admit latency in ms
- X-Redwood-Region-Spill: comma list of fallback regions (e.g., us-west,eu-central)
Example: ``X-Redwood-Queue-Depth: 42\nX-Redwood-Avg-Admit-Ms: 1213\nX-Redwood-Region-Spill: us-west,eu-central``
Liam: I like that. SDK behavior sketch:
```
if (resp.headers['X-Redwood-Queue-Depth'] > threshold) {
  backoff = min(maxBackoff, base * (1 + jitter()))
  if (resp.headers['X-Redwood-Region-Spill']) tryFallbackRegion()
}
```
Keep jitter broad enough to avoid synchronized retries.
Maya: We should also emit a compact admission token when we accept a request so downstream retries can carry a short-circuit hint (eg. `X-Redwood-Admit-Token: a1b2c3`). That lets clients preferentially reattach to the same pool if advised.
Sasha: Agreed. Two paths: 1) surface these headers ASAP in hosted API (opt-in via header toggle) and 2) add them to Dedicated control plane later (privacy/compliance checks). We need to be careful about exposing raw queue depths externally — maybe quantize and cap values (e.g., buckets: 0, 1-10, 11-50, 50+).
Liam: +1 on bucketing. Also add a `X-Redwood-Admit-Hint: low|med|high` as a privacy-safe summary.
Devex: SDK rollout plan thoughts: ship header parsing + exponential jitter backoff in minor release, opt-in behind `enable_admit_hints` default=false, then enable for 25% of traffic in hosted for 48h and monitor regressions.
Sasha: Telemetry: we need two metrics from SDKs when they see admit hints: `client.seen_admit_hint` and `client.followed_spill_to_region`. Add a tag for `hint_bucket`.
Maya: Also capture `request.size_tokens` and `retry_attempts` so we can correlate heavy users causing amplification.
Liam: Operationally, immediate mitigations for this incident: 1) enable regional spill routing to us-west for low-latency tolerant customers, 2) increase short-term autoscale headroom for eu-west by +2 nodes, 3) throttle background rerank jobs via job-scheduler. Can infra oncall run 1 & 2 now?
infra-bot: Runbook snippet: `curl -X POST https://ctl.internal/regions/eu-west/scale -d '{"delta_nodes":2}'` (requires ops token). Logged action id: run-1755-01
Maya: I'll draft the PR for header names + bucketing and include tests for header parsing and jitter distribution. Will also add a note about not logging raw queue depth in customer logs.
Sasha: Owners: Maya (header + SDK spec), Liam (sdk behavior + telemetry), Ops (execute scale + regional spill). Target: canary next Tue, full roll by Fri if metrics look good.
Liam: One more ask — add `X-Redwood-Server-Timestamp` to help diagnose clock skew when correlating client events.
Sasha: Good call.
Devex: I'm adding a short doc snippet to the SDK quickstart about how clients should handle admit hints and prefer region spillovers. Will include example pseudocode and suggested default jitter params.
Maya: Cool. I'll post a follow-up thread with the PR link and a small test harness for simulating a saturation wave.
Sasha: Thanks all. Let's keep this tight — these waves are the primary tail risk for cost and SLOs. (reacted :eyes:)
